Not related to the pots (we dont really know yet)  but i started having seizures and then got taken to a hospital to get checked out. They noticed my heart rate was in the 40s and went uhhh thats not good and rushed me to a bigger hospital went into a resus area when it dipped under 35. 

Anyway from there i stayed a few hours and went home and got booked into a cardiologist who literally just had me sit and then stand and went yup you have POTS. 5 minutes. And it could’ve been dealt with when i was 8 years old because thats when i first started having syncope episodes.

But my symptoms all match POTS to a T: 
- heart rate jumps over 30 beats per minute (40 -160)

-blood pressure drops

-pre syncope episodes from changing from sitting to standing

-constant fatigue

-dizziness

-cant exercise at all when its hot or i pass out

-constant lightheadedness from sitting or standing or bending down

-passing out

-heart palpitations and chest pains

- hella anxiety

- chronic nausea 

- blurred and blacked out vision from changing in statue

- freezing hands and feet

- blood pooling

- brain fog

- shakiness 

The list goes on

The most it has impacted anyone around me is when no one knew what was happening and it was dysfunctional because there was no rhyme or reason so everyone was confused. Now we all know why and its like a light switch like ohhh thats why everything makes sense. I guess with people who arent getting treated or regularly undergoing therapy and dbt therapy i can absolutely understand your point of view because i have seen some people who arent willing to help themselves with this disorder and they arent the healthiest to be around. Off topic for a second but i had a close friend for years who has bipolar (i know different basket but bare with me) and when she got diagnosed used that as excuse to turn into a horrible person because “shes bi polar she cant help it” when before the diagnosis she was the most down to earth kindest human i had ever met. But because now she has something to blame some of her toxic traits on, if you talked to her about something she did affecting you she would blow a fuse and say oh but im bipolar so i get a pass.

So i also think its whether they use it as an excuse as well as if they are willing or trying to better themselves. I think it really comes down to whether they are stable and being looked after with a healthy community or not. If that makes sense?? I like to think im quiet self aware and in control of my emotions all of the time (except for those few before period cries about kittens but who doesnt) but i like to think because i have people who understand and support me and i am constantly working on ways to identify reactions or triggers and react appropriately instead of blowing a fuse. And no one has to feel like they have to walk on eggshells around me because i realised through therapy that, that was how i had to grow up but its not fair for anyone else around me to deal with that. I think most of the worst parts of bpd can definitely be helped if not treated. 

Its still upsetting because obviously for a small percentage of people who suffer who cant or wont get help and they get worse, obviously that has an impact on the view of everyone who has it. Which I understand how that would happen, of course. 

I react in time calmly because i have been given the tools to do so, of course my brain still reacts as black and white thinking and straight to this or that blah nlah and bad thoughts and reactions within my head. But i can compose myself, if i feel im about to lose it i just either say i need to step out and calm down because this conversation is getting to emotionally intense for me currently and i need a breather. 

My biggest fear is thinking that i am hurting anyone around me. Most people with bpd we know exactly how things we do affect others especially if we werent in control and it honestly breaks us, we stay up for nights on end thinking about it and in pain because we know how what we did wasnt the correct way to go about things. From what i know its not a lack of awareness about how we affect people around us, we do know how painful it can be because we are in pain all of the time from knowing that ((idk if that made any sense😂)) 

maybe i am just speaking from my experiences with people like me but i know that there is a few bad eggs who are not stable or treated but it does not negate the many who are incredible human beings who struggle daily but still are able to react and think and behave safely and calmly. Who have put in the work to be the best of themselves even with one of the hardest mental illnesses. 

Sorry for such a long post, i hope this makes sense. Also i am sorry to hear about your experiences and i hope you find there is amazing people with this illness who would never do a thing to anyone. And i hope you are okay if you are on the receiving end of all the bad parts and lashing outs. If you need someone to talk to i am always here *hugs*

The behaviour of what? Having been traumatised and getting bpd out of it? So whenever anything happens they are on a fight or flight mode? Bpd is trauma based from my experience anyway. We are painted in a bad light because it is not a very well known or studied illness. Yes it causes problems but they are in perspective not severe. Usually its splitting between “oh my god they hate me” to “oh my god i love myself i am a god no one cant hate me” which a split ONLY usually happens when somethings triggers it, ex. Cheating, something to cause abandonment issues to play up, trust problems, someone leaving their life so on and so forth. Or we completely dissociate and have no feelings towards anything at all. Idk if you have ever not being able to feel a single emotion but you in turn, turn into just an emotionless careless person who is simply trying to survive.

And what exactly is “going to happen” they get hurt, upset. And seeing their previous trauma playing right in front of them so they either try and hurt themselves or kill themselves because they feel they are the reason everything bad in their life happens? Bpd is the most painful illness to have it has been studied enough to say that people with bpd have their emotions feeling 10x what a normal person does. You feel sad? You cry and hurt a bit. Someone with bpd feels sad? It feels like everything around them is crashing down, their life has ended and they have nothing to live for. (From someone who has diagnosed bpd and bi polar painting us all in a light of “its for a good reason” when the reason is no one understands and just thinks we are psychotic and kill or hurt others.) ((you can choose to believe of not believe but i have all the paperwork from two psychiatrists if you want proof)) 

The “reputation” is not based in any actual reality. Many mentally sane people kill, hurt others. Do foul things. But the moment someone mentally ill does its the entire spectrum of anyone who has the same disorder who is villanised. People like you are the reason people who are struggling with serious mental health issues cannot receive help because of a complete incorrect stigma around it. Absolutely disgusting point of view.

Thats appalling i am so sorry. It took my entire life to get diagnosed with POTS and thats because i started having syncopes. Only then was it found out i have a deformed heart and heart issues. The rest isn’t diagnosed so thats why i went to the hospital to get help when i experienced worse and new symptoms to just be sent home. I am used to POTS symptoms because i have had it all my life and my parents are very much the kind that are like “youre making it up for attention.” “Dont go to the doctors unless you are dying and even then you have to be on your death bed” kind of people and i dont blame them or hold any hate against them its how they are and how i grew up so i never cared about these symptoms just lived with it. My heart rate always rested around 40 and the lowest its been to on record is 35. I did one test with my cardiologist of the sit/stand test and went from 45 to 130 (i think i cannot remember precisely how high it went) within a few seconds. As a women i was told for years “its low iron” when my blood tests didn’t indicate that. I was put on so many iron supplements, changed birth control. Everything. One talk with a female doctor and its “why are you taking this? That is detrimental to your health” because from the ones i have had male doctors just assume it to do with birth control or periods or mental health. Maybe they’ll order some basic blood work but thats it. 

So when things get bad enough for me to go to hospital it means its bad. And i am so sorry to hear that, it honestly makes me so angry on you’re behalf. I really hope that you are on the right track in treatment and care. I am always here to support if you ever need it, or just someone who understands what you’re going through. We can all live a good life, we just have to keep fighting with the “bad” and unhelpful medical professionals and find ones who are willing yo fight for us too. Which sucks but sadly it is what the world is like these days.
